It is located in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}}.

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Soejimo district|ja|添下郡|zh|添下郡|qid=Q11560415}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1273537/1/44 |title=Engishiki |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. It is regarded nationwide as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|abstract|Q1107129|de|Sōja (Shintō)|fr|Sōja (shinto)|ja|総社|ko|소자 (신토)|simple|Sōja shrine|zh|總社|qid=Q1107129}} (principal shrine) of the god of {{ill|Metalsmith|az|Dəmirçilik|ce|Аьчкапхьар|da|Smed|de|Schmied|fa|متال اسمیت|he|מסגר|ja|鍛冶|nds|Smed|nl|Smid|nn|Smed|no|Smed|pl|Kowal|pnb|دھاتچی|sh|Kovač|simple|Smith (metalwork)|sl|Kovač|sr|Kovač metala|sv|Smed|tg|Оҳангар|tr|Demircilik|tt|Тимерче|uz|Temirchilik|qid=Q838566}}.

In ancient times, the shrine was located about 300 meters south of its present site, and it is said to have been transferred to its current location around the 3rd year of {{ill|Daiei (era)|fa|دایئی (دوره)|fr|Ère Daiei|ia|Daiei (era)|ja|大永|ko|다이에이 (연호)|no|Daiei (japansk æra)|ru|Тайэй|simple|Daiei (era)|sr|Даиеи (ера)|sv|Daiei (japansk era)|tr|Daiei (dönem)|zh|大永|qid=Q1193564}} (1523)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://jun-yu-roku.com/yamato-heguri-hachijo-sugata/ |title=Sugata Shrine |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>.

== History ==
Long ago, a beautiful goddess appeared from “Sugata Pond” in Nikaidō, {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ar|تيرني (نارا)|azb|تنری، نارا|ca|Tenri|ce|Тэнри|ceb|Tenri (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Tenri|eo|Tenri|es|Tenri (Nara)|eu|Tenri (Nara)|fa|تنری، نارا|fi|Tenri|fr|Tenri|gl|Tenri|id|Tenri, Nara|it|Tenri|ja|天理市|ko|덴리시|mg|Tenri|mzn|تنری، نارا|nl|Tenri|pl|Tenri|pt|Tenri|ro|Tenri|ru|Тэнри|simple|Tenri, Nara|sv|Tenri, Nara|tg|Тенри|tl|Tenri, Nara|tr|Tenri|tt|Тэнри|uk|Тенрі|ur|ٹینری، نارا|vi|Tenri, Nara|war|Tenri, Nara|zh|天理市|zh_classical|天理市|zh_min_nan|Tenri-chhī|zh_yue|天理|qid=Q502196}}. She rested for a while in Kagurada in Hachijō-chō, Yamatokōriyama City, and then went westward and took up residence there. Overnight, the place became a dense pine grove, and people began to call the area “Ichiya-matsu” (One-Night Pine). Thus, the present Sugata Shrine—also known as “Ichiya-matsu Tenjin” or “Hachijō Tenjin Shrine”—came to be enshrined there<ref>From the shrine notice board</ref>. The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Meiji Jinja Shiryō}} records: “The Saho River flows to the west, overlooking the banks of Sugata Pond. In the *Horigawa Hyakushu*<ref group="note">A poetry anthology from the late Heian period, likely compiled around the 2nd year of Chōji (1105).</ref>, it is written: ‘The lotus leaves on Sugata Pond, where the maiden dwells, bloom with a gentle heart.’ From this one may know that it was a place of scenic beauty.”

== Overview ==
The enshrined deity is Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto. There is also a theory that the deity is {{ill|Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|ja|天目一箇神|ko|아메노마히토쓰노카미|zh|天目一箇神|qid=Q10016750}}, an ancestor of Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto and regarded as a god of blacksmithing<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/815494/1/11 |title=Shingi Shiryō |access-date=2024-4-24}}</ref>. However, the {{ill|jinjameisaichou|ja|神社明細帳|qid=Q11590704}} of {{ill|Heguri district|ja|平群郡|zh|平群郡|qid=Q11483501}} (Hachijō Village in the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|ceb|Panahon sa Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} was under the jurisdiction of Heguri District and {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|ar|إيكوما|ca|Districte d'Ikoma|ceb|Ikoma-gun|es|Distrito de Ikoma|fa|شهرستان ایکوما، نارا|fr|District d'Ikoma|id|Distrik Ikoma, Nara|it|Distretto di Ikoma|ja|生駒郡|ko|이코마군|nl|Ikoma (district)|pl|Powiat Ikoma|ru|Икома (уезд)|zh|生駒郡|qid=Q971003}}, and was incorporated into {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kōriyama Town}} in 1953) records Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto as the enshrined deity<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://meta01.library.pref.nara.jp/opac/repository/repo/69/ |title=Heguri District Shrine Registry |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>. Sugata-hiko-no-Mikoto is the ancestor of the Sugata clan, and the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362}} states: “The Sugata no Obito are descendants of {{ill|Ame-no-Mahitotsu-no-Mikoto|ja|天目一箇神|ko|아메노마히토쓰노카미|zh|天目一箇神|qid=Q10016750|lt=Ame-no-Kushi-mahito-tsu-no-Mikoto}}.”

Before the early modern period, the shrine was also called Hachijō Tenjin Shrine or Ichiya-matsu Tenjin, and it enshrined {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}. A legend tells of a miracle in which a pine tree grew overnight, and part of the bark of the Ichiya Pine is {{ill|Votive offering|af|Votiewe offer|ar|نذر|azb|آداق (میفولوژی)|be|Воты|bg|Оброчна плочка|br|Arouez gouestl|ca|Ofrena|da|Votivgave|de|Votivgabe|el|Ανάθημα|es|Ofrenda votiva|et|Votiiv|eu|Zinopari|fa|ودیعه نذری|fi|Votiivilahja|fr|Offrande votive|gl|Ofrenda votiva|id|Persembahan nazar|it|Offerta votiva|ja|奉納|ko|봉헌물|lt|Votas|nl|Votiefgave|nn|Votivgåve|no|Votivgave|pl|Dar wotywny|ru|Вотивные предметы|sl|Votivni dar|sv|Votivgåva|uk|Вотивні предмети|vi|Lễ vật|zh|献祭|qid=Q2601788}} in the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|es|Haiden (sintoísmo)|fa|هایدن (شینتو)|fi|Haiden|fr|Haiden|id|Haiden (Shinto)|it|Haiden|ja|拝殿|mk|Хаиден (Шинто)|pl|Haiden|pt|Haiden|ru|Хайдэн|tr|Haiden (Şinto)|qid=Q3125745}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://yamatotk.web.fc2.com/kouriyama/sugata.htm |title=Sugata Shrine |access-date=2024-4-23}}</ref>. A stone lantern from the 5th year of {{ill|Genna|de|Genna (Ära)|es|Genna|fa|گننا|fr|Ère Genna|id|Genna|it|Genna|ja|元和 (日本)|ko|겐나|ru|Гэнна|simple|Genna|sr|Гена|sv|Genna|tr|Genna|zh|元和 (日本)|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} (1619) bears the inscription “Ichiya-matsu Kinrin-gū,” suggesting the existence of a {{ill|Jingū-ji|fr|Jingū-ji|it|Jingū-ji|ja|神宮寺|pl|Jingū-ji|ru|Дзингудзи|zh|神宮寺|qid=Q1074971}} called Ichiya-matsu Kinrin-ji. Its location is estimated to have been west of Kasuga Shrine in Nikaidō Kita-Sugata-chō, {{ill|Tenri, Nara|ar|تيرني (نارا)|azb|تنری، نارا|ca|Tenri|ce|Тэнри|ceb|Tenri (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Tenri|eo|Tenri|es|Tenri (Nara)|eu|Tenri (Nara)|fa|تنری، نارا|fi|Tenri|fr|Tenri|gl|Tenri|id|Tenri, Nara|it|Tenri|ja|天理市|ko|덴리시|mg|Tenri|mzn|تنری، نارا|nl|Tenri|pl|Tenri|pt|Tenri|ro|Tenri|ru|Тэнри|simple|Tenri, Nara|sv|Tenri, Nara|tg|Тенри|tl|Tenri, Nara|tr|Tenri|tt|Тэнри|uk|Тенрі|ur|ٹینری، نارا|vi|Tenri, Nara|war|Tenri, Nara|zh|天理市|zh_classical|天理市|zh_min_nan|Tenri-chhī|zh_yue|天理|qid=Q502196}}<ref group="note">Originally, “it was probably dedicated to Ame-no-Kushi-hitotsu-no-Mikoto” (from *Tenri City History*).</ref><ref name=":01">Tenri City History, Volume 1</ref>.

The {{ill|Honden|ar|هوندن (شنتو)|ca|Honden|cs|Honden|es|Honden|eu|Honden|fi|Honden|fr|Honden|id|Honden|it|Honden|ja|本殿|nl|Honden (shinto)|oc|Honden|pl|Honden|pt|Honden|ru|Хондэн|simple|Honden|th|ฮนเด็ง|tr|Honden|qid=Q2044994}} is built in the {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|es|Kasuga-zukuri|fr|Kasuga-zukuri|ja|春日造|ru|Касуга-дзукури|qid=Q3193781}} style, with a {{ill|Heiden (Shinto)|es|Heiden (sintoísmo)|fi|Heiden (šintolaisuus)|fr|Heiden (shinto)|id|Heiden (Shinto)|it|Heiden (architettura)|ja|幣殿|pt|Heiden (xintoísmo)|ru|Хэйдэн|tr|Heiden (Şinto)|qid=Q3076699}} installed between it and the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|es|Haiden (sintoísmo)|fa|هایدن (شینتو)|fi|Haiden|fr|Haiden|id|Haiden (Shinto)|it|Haiden|ja|拝殿|mk|Хаиден (Шинто)|pl|Haiden|pt|Haiden|ru|Хайдэн|tr|Haiden (Şinto)|qid=Q3125745}}. In front of the main hall stands a stone lantern inscribed “Before the Deity of Tenmangū,” indicating that the shrine was associated with {{ill|Tenjin faith|ja|天神信仰|ko|천신신앙|qid=Q66890725}}.

It is also thought to form a pair with {{ill|Sugatahime Shrine|ja|菅田比売神社|qid=Q134893097}}, another Shikinaisha of Soekami District located in Tsutsui-chō, Yamatokōriyama City (enshrining Sugata-hime-no-Mikoto and Ame-no-Kushi-mahito-tsu-no-Mikoto, two deities<ref>According to *Tokusen Shinmeichō* and the National Diet Library Search “Research on Shikinaisha, Vol. 2.”</ref>)<ref group="note">However, the Soekami District Shrine Registry lists only one deity: Izunome-no-Kami.</ref>.

== Annual festival ==
It was formerly held on October 28, but is now held on October 15.

It is jointly celebrated by Minami-Sugata, Kita-Sugata, Hachijō, Chōan-ji, Miyadō, Nukatabe, Nishimura, and other areas. During the {{ill|procession|ja|渡御|qid=Q11561919}} of the hosting household, it is customary for the Sugata clan of Minami-Sugata to proceed first<ref name=":01" />.
